LEARNING PATH · CLASS 41 · TIME & DAILY ROUTINE · AGES 4–5

Time & Daily Routine — forty-one cards that put your day in order.

Forty-one printable time cards for ages four to five, in five shelves: your day, the calendar, the parts of the day, the time words and the plan-and-patience skills. Every card carries its rule in words YOU can say back — first, next, last; now, soon, later; yesterday, today, tomorrow — and every card has its own short page that turns the rule into today’s practice. It all starts with the waving cover boy: your day has an order, and YOU can say it.

Start with Morning →Back to the Learning Path ↗
HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

One rule. The child says it. Then the day does the teaching.

Every card prints one time idea the way a four-year-old meets it: the day’s five morning steps, the week’s seven names, the short hand that points to the hour, the waiting that takes a breath. The short pages quote each card’s rule word for word and add one thing to try today that takes less than a minute to set up — walking your school day in first-next-last order, counting the sleeps to a special day, freezing when the word is stop. Time words grow the same way the cards run — small, happy and repeated.

The shelves follow the day. The my-day shelf walks YOUR routine from wake-up to bedtime and back to work. The calendar shelf holds the big time names — seven days, twelve months, weekdays and the weekend, and the countdown that makes waiting fun. The day-parts shelf reads the sky and the clock: morning to midnight, the meal times, the time helpers. The time-words shelf is the word family — now, soon, later, before, during, after, first, second, third. And the own-it shelf is where planning lives: plan my day, chores in order, when plans change, and the patience to wait.

AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where the time learning grows.

Everyday habits in Class 32 · Ages 4–5 ↗Weather & seasons in Class 34 · Ages 4–5 ↗Story order in Sequence Stories · Ages 3–5 ↗The Daily Routine & Times of Day sheets in First Glance · Ages 2–5 ↗The parents’ shelf in the library · All 41 cards to print ↗

Class 32 builds the everyday habits this day runs on, Class 34 walks the seasons your calendar counts through, and the Sequence Stories class puts four-picture stories in the same first-next-last order these cards teach. The First Glance Daily Routine and Times of Day sheets hold the youngest version of the same words. And when the cards need printing, parents will find the whole deck on the parents’ shelf in the flashcards library — download and print buttons under every card, no extra pages to hop through.

Your day has an order, and YOU can say it. Every card here hands the time words to you — the waking, the waiting, the planning — and your grown-up’s whole job is to keep the day calm enough to notice them.
